**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **Searches run:** "most favored", "most favoured", "no less favorable", "favorable", "favourable", "favor", "comparable", "terms at least as", "match" — no MFN-type language anywhere in the agreement. The only "favor" hit (p0648, § 13.2.2) concerns successors/assignees, not comparative terms.
- **Targeted read:** Section 5.9 (In-License Agreements), the planner's flagged risk area, runs in our favour: Harpoon may not enter third-party IP agreements without our consent (5.9.1), AbbVie holds the first right to negotiate third-party licenses (5.9.2), and Harpoon must disclose future in-licensed rights which we may elect to take up (5.9.3).
- **Direction check:** nothing obliges AbbVie to give Harpoon terms no less favourable than those granted to third parties, or to match a third-party offer. This satisfies the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so the rule is compliant rather than "missing" — absence of an MFN burden is exactly what the playbook wants.
